subject: Everwell GPU pool sizing & stair-step commit options
messages:
From: Oliver Klein <oliver.klein@everwell.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated sizing and commit questions for Everwell

Hi Sean / Marissa,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Procurement looped me in to get numbers for a reserved GPU commit rather than the hosted API — we need predictable throughput and lower unit economics. A few details on our side:

- Typical steady-state: ~120 qps (text generation requests) with average prompt+response ~4k tokens.
- Peak concurrency: sustained ~450 concurrent requests during business hours; occasional spikes up to ~750 for major campaigns.
- Context: most sessions use 4k context; ~15% of requests hit 8k context with longer system prompts.
- Model mix: primary model is a fine-tuned 13B for chat + a smaller 3B for embeddings and low-latency retrieval.
- Latency target: p95 generation <250ms for the 13B model.

We are looking for: a recommended GPU pool size for a Dedicated deployment, an example stair-step reserved commit (3 / 6 / 12 month ramp) with associated discount tiers, and any notes on throughput guarantees or burst capacity. Can you also confirm what we should expect for cold-cache vs warm-cache behavior when many users have long contexts?

I attached our SRE requirements doc (see stub). Happy to hop on a call if helpful — procurement asked for a ballpark by end of week.

Thanks,
Oliver
Head of Platform
Everwell AI

Attachment: SRE-requirements.pdf (stub)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-07-19T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing and commit questions for Everwell

Hi Oliver — thanks, this is very helpful. Quick clarifying questions before we size:

1) Of the 120 steady-state qps, what percentage are short-turn responses (<=512 tokens) vs long responses (>1024 tokens)?
2) For the 15% that hit 8k context, are those evenly distributed across users or concentrated in a small subset of heavy sessions?
3) Do you expect the peak 750 to be sustained for more than a few minutes, or is it mostly short bursts?

High-level we can definitely design a stair-step commit that starts smaller and ramps. I'll loop in Marissa for workload sizing and Ben on pricing/discounting. Meanwhile, for warm-cache behavior: our runtime keeps KV cache hot per-session and you should expect 2-4x better token throughput when the cache is shared (e.g., same session or repeated system prompts). Cold-cache long-context requests will push down qps and require extra GPU headroom for the same latency SLO.

Propose a 30 minute call today if you have availability — otherwise we'll send a consolidated recommendation by EOD.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-07-19T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated sizing and commit questions for Everwell

Sean / Ben — quick sizing note based on Oliver's numbers and our Dedicated runtime benchmarks. High-level recommendation and rationale below.

Summary recommendation (recommended pool architecture):
- Baseline pool: 6x H100-class GPUs (primary serving nodes) to cover steady-state 120 qps for the 13B model at warm-cache assumptions (shared sessions, batching).
- Burst/scale workers: additional 4x H100-class GPUs in a burst pool to absorb sustained peak concurrency and spikes (handles additional 200-300 concurrent sessions at near-warm-cache).
- Redundancy / cache replication: 2x GPUs reserved for KV cache redundancy/lead replica and maintenance (ensures no single-point-of-failure during rolling updates).
- Total recommended capacity for initial commit: 12 GPUs (6 baseline + 4 burst + 2 redundancy).

Throughput notes and latency sensitivity:
- 8k contexts reduce per-GPU throughput by roughly 35-45% vs 4k; since ~15% of traffic is 8k, model this as a 6-8% effective drop on the aggregated qps.
- Cold-cache long-context requests can reduce effective pool capacity briefly; plan for headroom of ~15% to maintain p95 <250ms during cache misses.
- With the 12 GPU architecture above and warm-cache behavior, we estimate sustained p95 <250ms for 120 qps and headroom for typical peaks to ~500 concurrent. Spikes to 750 will rely on burst pool scaling and queued latency allowance — if Everwell needs hard SLA coverage at 750 sustained, we'd move to a 16 GPU commit.

Stair-step commit suggestion (pricing bands, non-binding):
- Phase A (months 0-3): commit 6 GPUs. Good for pilot and tight cost control.
- Phase B (months 4-6): expand to 10 GPUs (6 baseline + 2 burst + 2 redundancy).
- Phase C (months 7-12): move to 12 GPUs (target production).

Discount guidance (example, subject to PO and term):
- 3-month commit: base price, minimal discount (0-5%).
- 6-month commit: target 8-12% discount over base per-GPU rate.
- 12-month commit: target 15-22% discount; higher discounts available for larger pool sizes or prepayment.

Bursting and guarantees:
- We can include a burst buffer (ephemeral GPUs) for short spikes at no additional monthly commit cost up to a configured limit (e.g., 2x baseline for up to 10 minutes / hour). Extended bursts will be billed as overage or require higher committed tiers.
- SLA: we can offer latency-backed targets on the committed baseline capacity. For strict SLA at sustained 750 concurrency, need increased committed capacity (we should quote 16 GPUs for that case).

Attachments and calculations: I used their stated mix and typical 13B per-GPU throughput from our lab: ~20-25 qps per H100-equivalent at 4k warm-cache for the tuned runtime; adjust down for 8k and cold-cache as noted. I also added a short CSV of session shape assumptions (everwell-workload-snapshot-0701.csv attached as a stub).

Next steps: Ben, can you validate discount bands and give a ballpark monthly price per GPU for 6 / 10 / 12 GPU commits? Sean, I can prepare a one-page capacity diagram and a brief explanation of warm vs cold-cache behavior for Oliver.

-Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: everwell-workload-snapshot-0701.csv (stub)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@everwell.ai
Date: 2027-07-19T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed Dedicated commit & sizing — Everwell (summary)

Oliver — thanks again. Summary of our recommended path based on Marissa's sizing and internal pricing guidance:

- Recommended initial architecture: 12 GPUs (6 baseline serving, 4 burst workers, 2 redundancy/cache replicas). This covers steady 120 qps with p95 <250ms at warm-cache and provides capacity for routine peaks to ~500 concurrent. Spikes to 750 are supported as short bursts; for sustained 750 concurrency we recommend 16 GPUs and can include that option in the proposal.

- Stair-step commit we suggest: 6 GPUs (months 0-3) -> 10 GPUs (months 4-6) -> 12 GPUs (months 7-12). This lets you start with a pilot and ramp as traffic stabilizes.

- Pricing snapshot (ballpark, non-binding): per-GPU monthly base rate X, with discounts by term: 3-month ~0-5% off base, 6-month ~8-12% off, 12-month ~15-22% off. Ben will follow up with exact numbers and an ARR calculation depending on prepay vs monthly billing.

- Burst policy: short burst buffer up to 2x baseline for limited intervals (configurable). Extended bursts billed as overage unless you step up the committed tier.

I'll attach a short one-page and a draft proposal for procurement. Can we schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk procurement through the ramp and confirm contract terms? Proposed times: 10am PST or 2pm PST.
